messages:
jordan: heads-up — ran the overnight perf sweep with high long-context traffic. saw a repeatable pattern where KV page reclamation stalls coincide with continuous-batching merge waits; flamegraphs look ugly.
maya: can you paste the flamegraph or top pprof numbers? rough metrics help.
jordan: short pprof top:
```
(pprof) top5
45.1%  kv_reclaim_page
18.3%  batch_merge_wait
12.0%  evict_scan
6.7%   kv_slot_lock
```
Callers show schedule_batch -> batch_merge_wait -> kv_slot_lock -> kv_reclaim_page.
rishi: is this on dev single-gpu or only on multi-tenant hosts? reproducible locally?
jordan: repros on my devbox with synthetic longctx workload: `loadgen --longctx --qps 400 --prefix-reuse 0.75`. Only triggers when merged batch size frequently > 8 and prefix reuse high.
emily: sounds like fragmentation + prefetch thrash. did you try turning off prefetch to see effect?
jordan: yes — disabling prefetch drops CPU in kv_reclaim_page by ~60% but increases p99 latency by 5-10ms. hypothesis: prefetch races with batch-merge: prefetch causes page loads/evictions while head-of-line batch is waiting on a merge, so the head gets stuck waiting for pages reclaimed by a competing batch.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled canary `kvcache/slot-fix` to 10% at 03:12 UTC :eyes:
maya: we should emit a head-of-line metric (per-batch hol_block_ms) and maybe fallback to split the merge when hol_block_ms > threshold.
rishi: we already emit kvcache.reclaim.ms and batch.merge.wait.ms; adding a per-batch hol_latency histogram is straightforward — will open PR to add kvcache.hol_ms (histogram)
jordan: heap profile (allocs) attached in logs shows pinned pages growth: `pinned_pages 1.2GB -> 1.8GB over 1h`. top alloc callers: `decode_prefix()`, `embed_cache()`. suggests slots being held longer during merges.
emily: strategy idea — optimistic split: if merge wait > 30ms and head batch is blocked by slot lock held by a later batch, split the merge into two smaller merges so head can proceed. prototypeable.
jordan: :thumbsup: I'll run nightly with env `REDWOOD_EXPERIMENTAL_SPLIT=true` and collect hol histograms. also trying a small kernel-selection tweak to reduce per-token CPU in reclaim path.
maya: also add alert: `kvcache.pinned_ratio > 0.6` sustained over 5m -> page the oncall. that will help catch regressions early.
rishi: tracking as RFC#421 — covers metrics + split heuristic. assigning to @rishi for metric work and @emily for prototype split.
jordan: saved traces and flamegraphs to `/tmp/kvhol/3250012345.tar.gz`. uploading to benchdash and will paste link when available. thx all.
